policy_notes: Back slot with positive cargo: preserve shell itemSize; round rows up after scaling.

Vanilla clothing in the clothing_cargo_slots (Body, Legs, Vest, Hips) with positive cargo: itemsCargoSize grows about clothing_cargo_multiplier-fold with rows rounded up, never above clothing_cargo_cap times the stock cells, width at most 10 and grown only when no extra row fits; classes already at or above cap times the slot median stay unchanged; zero cargo stays zero; itemSize, weight and insulation never change and no grid ever shrinks, so stored contents always fit. Hats, masks, gloves, boots, stack and variety-pack clothing are untouched (stack classes that inherit a changed vanilla grid are pinned to their stock cargo).
All other positive cargo, including inherited cargo: never shrink itemSize or change cargo.
General area 3/4: shorten longer dimension by one; square 2x2 becomes 1x2 by shrinking width. Area decreases by two for this square, following the owner's explicit 2x2 example.

Area 2: medical; consumables (food/drink/material/seed addons or explicit matches/lighter/candle/filter includes); or tools strictly below 500g (tools/navigation/handheld optics/traps addons). Weapon attachment slots exclude an item from general small-item sizing; attachment_scale separately uses vanilla references.
Only scope=2 inventory descendants are shrunk. Every backpack definition, including hidden bases and inherited variants, receives its own vanilla-derived cargo override so scaling never compounds.
Unknown ancestry, ambiguous defining addon, and unsupported numeric dimensions fail closed; original addon requiredAddons are preserved.
Public vanilla diagnostic variants follow the same size rules as their family; changing a public parent must not silently resize excluded or hidden descendants.

Ancestry selects medical/consumable/tool groups before addon hints. Inventory slot and original weight constrain eligibility. Source list order breaks ties after CfgPatches dependencies; disabled sources are audited but never emitted.

Workshop aliases resolve in tools/package/inventory_sources.py. Committed addon/config output is rejected if it contains restricted provider tokens; package-only overrides remain under tools/package until disposable release injection. All size inputs precede HC overrides; scaling never compounds.

notes: Only public non-cargo mod attachments with slots used by observed weapon hosts, or native magazine slots / Magazine_Base ancestry, qualify. Native classes (including stack reopenings) and ammunition/firearms are untouched.

Vanilla CfgWeapons attachments arrays derive the native slot set; all installed weapon hosts derive eligibility for custom slots. Custom aliases are ordered configurable mappings to native reference slots, not a guessed eligibility list. Unknown mappings are reported as missing_reference.

References use public vanilla itemSize values before any HC or Workshop overrides. largest_area (default), median_area (lower median), smallest_area select an actual vanilla w x h pair; area ties sort width, height, then class name. Multiple compatible slots take the largest reference.
area_or_dimension (default), area, dimension control oversize detection. Each resulting dimension is min(original, reference): never rotate or enlarge an item, even when input orientation differs.

Magazine capacity fields are tried in order, using the first positive finite value. Bands are inclusive upper bounds followed by null for infinity; defaults <=10, <=30, <=60, <=100 and >100 keep ordinary drums separate from 200-round boxes. Unknown capacity stays unchanged and is reported.
Quivers, CO2 and shock cartridges do not define bullet-magazine reference sizes. Their own vanilla sizes remain unchanged. These reference exceptions are configurable by class.

Optic kinds match ordered exact ancestors, configurable ancestor patterns (including self), or slots first, then smallest positive inherited OpticsInfo opticsZoomMin/Max bands (<=0.08 long; <=0.15 compact; otherwise reflex); constant arithmetic expressions are parsed without executing code. Missing zoom falls back to compact. Night optics use their explicit vanilla ancestry group; thresholds and mappings are policy assumptions pending in-game review.

Both weapon packs are enabled for attachment_scale only. Their reviewed overrides and hashes live under tools/package; release injects them and a separate HollowCountryAttachmentScale patch into the disposable HCX config. Base HCX requiredAddons does not depend on the packs. Generation reads tools/setup/workshop_mods.json by Workshop identity: only declared sources are loaded, and declared packs require installed readable configs for --check. Removing a pack requires --refresh-review --write against that stack to remove its overrides and dependencies; release fails if the committed table or reviewed stack overrides name an absent source.

Hidden/excluded descendants without an intervening explicit size are pinned to their original dimensions. All generated blocks and the pack table must match regeneration byte-for-byte. Release refuses a table with stale rules or generator hashes.

Grenades/explosives stay outside attachment sizing even if a mod weapon advertises their carrying slot. Custom slot aliases may also match configured ancestor patterns (self included); broad short patterns are explicit policy and require review when the installed stack changes.
